parts:

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server now available for early testing
parts:
If you're requesting http://hostname:3838/, then this happens if there isn't an index.html file in your site directory.

If you're requesting http://hostname:3838/my-app-name, then please make sure you that your app directory is located in the site directory and has a directory name that looks like my-app-name.shiny. This seems to be the cause of a lot of confusion so far unfortunately.

I am having problems connecting to my shiny server install too.  The server starts and listens to port 3838, but browser says connection interrupted. I cannot find any log. I tried to run the server under root in case it might be a permission problem, but no luck.
On Wed, Jan 16, 2013 at 12:40 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

Hi Ryan, do you see any log files in /var/shiny-server/log?


On Wed, Jan 16, 2013 at 1:17 PM, Ryan Hafen <rha...@gmail.com> wrote:
This is excellent news!  I've installed it on 3 RHEL5 machines.  It works fine on 2 but doesn't work on the other. 

I have an index.html file in the /var/shiny-server/www directory that displays fine, meaning that node is working, but I took an example from the shiny tutorial as a test app and when I navigate to the app, I get the following:

An error has occurred

The application failed to start.

The application exited during initialization.

All files in the www directory have 777 permissions.

In the console, it says 

[2013-01-16 13:07:45.450] [INFO] shiny-server - Error getting worker: Error: The application exited during initialization.

Any suggestions on how to proceed to diagnose this?




On Monday, January 14, 2013 1:27:49 AM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
Shiny Server is now available for early testing. Setup instructions are here:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server

You will need root access to a Linux server (we've mostly been testing on Ubuntu, but CentOS 6 should work as well).

Up to this point we have had hardly any field testing of Shiny Server other than running on glimmer.rstudio.com, so proceed at your own risk.

--
--
